Issue: Tutorial steps 3-5 pointed to empty or inactive UI
Evidence: Review screenshots showed tutorial callouts around blank margin/inspect regions instead of live features.
Likely Cause: Tutorial used DOM selectors with broad fallback rectangles; early story state did not always have media/inspect surfaces available.
Decision: Added tutorial-only visual demos for interactive text/media/inspect states; tightened step copy and fallback targeting without mutating playback state.
Status: Improved; still needs another screenshot review on real desktop/mobile flows.

Issue: Spacebar triggered focused controls or page scroll instead of playback
Evidence: After clicking buttons or timed text, pressing Space could re-trigger the last control or scroll the page.
Likely Cause: Mouse/touch clicks left focus on buttons or role=button timed text; global Space handler skipped too many interactive targets.
Decision: Blur pointer-activated controls and timed text; changed global Space logic so timed text/inline media clicks route Space back to playback unless typing or in modal/keyboard-focused control.
Status: Improved; user-reported text-click scroll issue addressed in follow-up.

Issue: Mobile media peeks felt like buggy one-time flashes
Evidence: Active cue previews faded quickly and only appeared the first time a cue was reached.
Likely Cause: Mobile peek state tracked shown cue IDs permanently and auto-collapsed too quickly.
Decision: Extended peek duration and transitions; changed repeat policy so peeks can reappear when a cue is replayed or seeked back to its start.
Status: Improved; still needs mobile hands-on validation.

Issue: Progress bar media markers lacked affordance
Evidence: Markers were clickable and worked, but their meaning was not legible enough.
Likely Cause: Tiny marker-only UI had aria/title labels but little visible explanation.
Decision: Added hover/focus tooltips, clearer aria/title text, active/reached states, and expanded-control hint that gold dots jump to synced media.
Status: Improved; mobile affordance may need a later dedicated hint pattern.

Issue: Playback and inspect labels were too vague or technical
Evidence: Open and Inspect GIF/Chart/Identity did not clearly communicate actions.
Likely Cause: Microcopy reflected implementation concepts more than user intent.
Decision: Renamed Open to Controls; changed Inspect chart/media/identity to View chart/media/visual; softened GIF active to Visual cue/Now showing style language.
Status: Improved; full playback controls clarity remains a separate pass.

Issue: Segment media indicators were cluttered and too segment-local
Evidence: Left rail markers were visible but not intuitive; split team previews only showed media for the first audio-text segment.
Likely Cause: Each segment rendered only its own mediaCues, so continuation segments broke the team-preview continuity; multiple cues overloaded the rail.
Decision: Grouped rail markers by media type with counts; first segment in a continuation run now advertises media cues from its continuation segment too; continuation segment rails are suppressed.
Status: Improved; visual language still needs more UX review.

Issue: GIF/media sizing was inconsistent and sometimes cropped key content
Evidence: First GIF cue looked vertically large and later the contained GIF/image felt obscured by the card crop.
Likely Cause: Inline media used broad cover-style sizing for GIF/video cues.
Decision: Normalized inline moment sizing; changed GIF/video media fit toward contain with a taller 16:11 frame; preserved explicit mediaFit support for future overrides.
Status: Partially improved; user is not fully satisfied with GIF sizing and it needs another design pass.

Issue: Older inline media links conflicted with timeline media cues
Evidence: Hyperlinked GIF/image moments could linger or be hidden behind active cued charts, including the Taco Bell cardigan image.
Likely Cause: Inline links used a temporary custom event path separate from timeline media cue priority.
Decision: Inline media now renders with priority alongside active timeline cues; old GIF-ish inline entries were normalized; Taco Bell cardigan restored as static photo cue.
Status: Improved; long-term overlap policy for inline media versus timeline media still needs product design.

Issue: Mobile media previews only appeared once per cue
Evidence: Replaying or clicking back into a section did not show the preview again.
Likely Cause: The component stored every shown mobile cue ID in a permanent Set for the session.
Decision: Replaced permanent suppression with last-cue gating and replay-from-cue-start detection.
Status: Improved; should be verified with repeated seek/play on mobile.

Issue: Active media label wording felt too literal
Evidence: Labels like GIF active exposed implementation detail.
Likely Cause: Cue type labels were generated directly from media type.
Decision: Changed motion cue labels and data kickers toward Visual cue and Now showing.
Status: Improved.

Issue: Debugging media state was hard during UX review
Evidence: Manual review needed current time, active segment, active cue, upcoming cue, and media count without mutating state.
Likely Cause: No read-only media/debug overlay existed.
Decision: Added compact ?debug=media HUD showing playback time, active segment/cue, cue range, upcoming cue, cue count, playback/mute/inspect state.
Status: Resolved for dev-only debugging.

Issue: Early hero area did not demonstrate media cue sync
Evidence: Original review noted sync was not obvious until first body preview; suggested moving or duplicating hero image into media system.
Likely Cause: No hero default margin media existed and this pass prioritized later urgent fixes.
Decision: Not addressed in this thread beyond tutorial visual aids and existing early Thunder cue work from prior pass.
Status: Open.

Issue: Full playback control panel needs a separate clarity pass
Evidence: Expanded controls are functional but still not fully intuitive.
Likely Cause: Controls have accumulated transport/speed/scrub concepts without a dedicated information architecture pass.
Decision: Only immediate label and marker-hint improvements were made.
Status: Open.

Issue: Full lint failures remain outside UX scope
Evidence: Targeted lint still reports React compiler setState-in-effect/exhaustive-deps issues in existing playback/media effects.
Likely Cause: Pre-existing hook architecture conflicts with stricter React Compiler lint rules.
Decision: No broad lint cleanup was attempted; builds pass.
Status: Open technical debt.

Issue: Mobile chart preview required one extra tap before focused inspect
Evidence: Latest mobile screenshot sequence showed chart preview opening into a similar companion sheet before the user could reach the focused chart view.
Likely Cause: Chart cues used the same mobile peek-to-sheet flow as companion media, even though charts need inspect as the primary payoff.
Decision: Chart peeks now open inspect mode directly while non-chart media still uses the companion sheet path.
Status: Improved; verify across chart cues and non-chart media cues.

Issue: Mobile chart inspect felt like an accidentally clipped chart instead of an explorable canvas
Evidence: Inspect screenshot showed a useful zoom level but the chart opened uncentered with only part of the chart visible and weak overflow affordance.
Likely Cause: The inspect layout enlarged chart content via a scrollable frame but did not center the viewport or clearly signal horizontal exploration.
Decision: Auto-centered scrollable chart inspect frames on open; added visible scrollbar styling and edge shadows; removed forced tall SVG behavior that created excess blank chart space.
Status: Improved; still needs hands-on mobile validation for discoverability.

Issue: Inspect chart sequences did not autoplay by default
Evidence: Animated/state-driven chart inspect required the user to press Play Sequence before seeing the chart progression.
Likely Cause: Overlay playback existed but initialized paused and used technical sequence wording.
Decision: Inspect chart animation now starts looping locally by default at a faster rate with Pause animation/Play animation labels; story playback remains paused and unaffected.
Status: Improved.

Issue: Mobile playback markers felt visually oversized
Evidence: Media cue dots helped navigation but dominated the compact playback bar on mobile.
Likely Cause: Marker visuals were nearly as prominent as primary controls in a tight mini-player layout.
Decision: Reduced marker and mini-bar visual weight while preserving tappable hit area; hid redundant percent text on narrow mobile.
Status: Improved; broader playback control IA remains open.

Issue: Written text did not clearly reveal attached media moments
Evidence: Users could see section rails and progress markers, but could not scan the prose and tell which paragraph owned the next chart/GIF/image cue.
Likely Cause: Media indicators were rendered at segment/card level rather than aligned with timed paragraph ownership.
Decision: Added subtle left-gutter paragraph media anchors grouped by media kind/count; anchors strengthen for active/upcoming cues and click to the cue's absolute timeline time while preserving section rail and progress markers.
Status: Improved; needs desktop/mobile visual QA for density and clarity.

Issue: Mobile chart inspect still felt desktop-framed
Evidence: Mobile chart inspect was improved but still read as a wide desktop chart inside a vertical phone frame.
Likely Cause: Inspect CSS relied mainly on fixed-width horizontal overflow and centering.
Decision: Kept chart internals intact and adjusted inspect wrapper CSS: tighter vertical frame, reduced chart text density, responsive max width, visible scroll affordance, and preserved local autoplay/pause behavior.
Status: Improved; still not a full mobile-native chart rewrite.

Issue: Mini-player media markers were section-scoped while the track remained global
Evidence: The mini-player bar represented the full story while markers represented only the current team preview, creating mostly empty track space and a scope mismatch.
Likely Cause: Cue markers were filtered by logical section but fill/playhead still used global playback progress and global duration.
Decision: Made the compact mini-player track section-local using logical section start/end; marker positions and click-to-seek now share the same local visual scope while seeking remains absolute timeline-based.
Status: Improved; expanded controls keep their existing broader navigation behavior.

Issue: Media cue objects needed logical section ownership for scoped UI
Evidence: Section-scoped marker logic needed a stable cue-to-section relationship that would survive multi-clip previews.
Likely Cause: Timeline media cues only carried source segment IDs; section ownership was inferred indirectly.
Decision: Normalized media cues now include sectionId and a future-friendly story layer default; normalized segments also carry parent section playback bounds and adjacent section metadata.
Status: Improved; future source/utility/sponsored layers remain unimplemented by design.

Issue: Mini-player media cue markers were too tiny after section scoping
Evidence: Once scoped to the current section, markers were more relevant but still too small to read or tap confidently on mobile.
Likely Cause: Earlier marker sizing prioritized reducing global clutter before the track became section-local.
Decision: Increased marker size and tap target, added a separate slim playhead cap so playback position is distinct from cue dots, and added modest active/next cue emphasis.
Status: Improved; keep watching for overcrowding in media-dense sections.

Issue: Section-by-section navigation was hidden in expanded controls
Evidence: Users could not clearly see that READiscover supports moving by team preview/chapter from the default mini-player.
Likely Cause: Prev/Next transport existed only in the drawer and operated on raw segment/audio clip traversal.
Decision: Added always-visible compact Prev/Play/Next controls to the mini-player that navigate by adjacent logical story section start; first/last states are disabled/softened and playback continuity is preserved via existing jumpToSegment behavior.
Status: Improved; expanded drawer segment transport remains unchanged for now.
